title: Can warfarin dosing approaches be compared from clinic records? A pre-specified records profile and decision rule in a three-site anticoagulation clinic
abstract: Background: a paper nomogram and a computer-assisted dosing tool are used side by side in one anticoagulation clinic, and standardisation is planned. Methods: a four-week profile of INR and dose records at three clinics, with a pre-specified rule for choosing between a records comparison and a randomised comparison, and a primary outcome fixed in advance. Results and conclusions will be written after the profile.
introduction: Standardising dosing practice without local evidence risks choosing on enthusiasm. A recorded search for comparisons of these approaches in pharmacist-led clinics returned no records, and the clinic's own records have never been checked for completeness.
methods: All patients on warfarin in a four-week window; extraction of INR dates, entry dates where known, doses, testing mode and four case-mix variables inside the hospital network; calculability defined as no INR gap longer than 56 days; decision rule stated before extraction.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present calculability by clinic and testing mode, entry delays where recorded, and the design chosen under the pre-stated rule.
discussion: The discussion will state whether a records comparison is defensible, what the profile implies for patients who test at home, and what a randomised comparison would require.
limitations: Four weeks of data; completeness may improve while it is being measured; no comparison of dosing quality is made in this step.
conclusion: To be written after the profile; it will report fitness of the records and the design chosen, not which approach is better.
summary: Draft report of the records profile and decision rule, with results left empty.
